Dixon]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Carol Moseley Braun]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) | turnout = 74.84% }} {{Elections in Illinois}} The '''1992 United States Senate election in Illinois''' was held on November 3, 1992. Democratic incumbent [[Alan J. Dixon]] ran for re-election to a third term, but he was defeated in the Democratic primary by [[Carol Moseley Braun]], who won the general election. Until [[2022 United States Senate election in Illinois|2022]], this was the last time the same party won Illinois's Class 3 Senate seat in two or more consecutive elections. Primary elections took place on March 17, 1992.{{cite web |title=State of Illinois official vote cast at the primary election held on ... |url=https://archive.org/details/stateofillinoiso1992illi/mode/2up |publisher=Illinois State Board of Elections |access-date=7 April 2020}} Braun defeated Dixon and Albert Hofeld. As of 2026, Dixon is the last elected incumbent Democratic senator to lose renomination in a primary.{{efn|In April 2009, after serving in the Senate as a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] for 29 years, Senator [[Arlen Specter]] of Pennsylvania switched to the Democratic Party in anticipation of a difficult primary challenge in [[2010 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|2010]]. Specter ultimately lost to [[Joe Sestak]] in [[2010 United States Senate Democratic primary election in Pennsylvania|the Democratic primary]] on May 18.}} Braun made history by becoming the first African American senator who was a woman or member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]]. Braun was also both the first African American and the first woman elected senator from the state of Illinois. ==Background== The primaries and general elections coincided with those for other federal elections ([[1992 United States presidential election in Illinois|president]] and [[1992 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois|House]]), as well as those for [[1992 Illinois elections#State elections|state offices]]. For the primaries, turnout was 35.20%, with 2,064,347 votes cast. For the general election, turnout was 74.84%, with 4,939,557 votes cast.{{cite web |title=State of Illinois official vote cast at the general election .. |url=https://archive.org/details/stateofillinois1992illi/mode/2up |publisher=Illinois State Board of Elections |access-date=7 April 2020}} ==Democratic primary== === Candidates === * [[Carol Moseley Braun]], [[Cook County Recorder of Deeds|Cook County recorder of deeds]] and former state representative * [[Alan J. He was a moderate Democrat who recently voted to confirm [[Clarence Thomas]] to the [[United States Supreme Court|Supreme Court]].{{Cite news | url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/08/16/AR2005081601919.html | title = Democrats Feel Heat From Left On Roberts | author = Charles Babington and Dan Balz | date = August 17, 2005 | work = [[The Washington Post]] | publisher = [[Washington Post Company]] | quote = Nan Aron, president of the Alliance for Justice, said [...] 'History shows us that voters turned on Alan Dixon for his vote on Clarence Thomas and voters gave Arlen Specter the toughest reelection of his life.' | page = A01 }} Braun, a black woman and known reformist liberal, got a large share of black, liberal, and women voters ("The Year of the Woman"). In addition, she carried [[Cook County, Illinois]], by far the most populated county in the state. Another factor was the third candidate in the race, multi-millionaire attorney Al Hofeld. Hofeld drew away some of the moderate and conservative Democrats who normally supported Dixon. He also spent a lot of money running advertisements attacking Dixon, weakening his support. ==Republican primary== [[Richard S. Williamson]] ran unopposed in the Republican primary. {{Election box begin no change | title = Republican Primary, United States Senate, 1992{{Cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/stateofillinoiso1992illi#page/6 |title = United States Senator |publisher=Illinois State Board of Elections | access-date=November 21, 2015}}}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | party = Republican Party (United States) | candidate = [[Richard S. Williamson]] | votes = 608,079 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 608,079 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== === Candidates === * [[Carol Moseley Braun]], [[Cook County Recorder of Deeds|Cook County recorder of deeds]] and former state representative (Democratic) * John Justice (Populist) * Kathleen Kaku (Socialist Workers) * Chad Koppie, farmer, former [[Rutland Township, Kane County, Illinois|Rutland Township]] trustee, and retired commercial airline pilot (Independent) * Alan J. Port (New Alliance) * Andrew B. Spiegel (Libertarian) * [[Richard S. Williamson]], former [[Assistant Secretary of State for International Organization Affairs|assistant U.S. secretary of state for international organization affairs]] (Republican) * Charles A. Winter (Natural Law) === Results === Moseley Braun won the 1992 Illinois Senate Race by a fairly comfortable margin. Moseley Braun did well as expected in [[Cook County]] home of [[Chicago]]. Williamson did well in the Chicago collar counties, and most northern parts of the state. Moseley Braun had a surprisingly strong showing in southern Illinois, which Republicans had come to dominate in the last several decades.
